newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing says sees no need for German rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Issing says sees no need for German rate hike.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Thursday he saw no need at the moment for a German interest rate hike and that there were no signs at the moment of domestic inflationary pressure.
"There are no signs of inflation in Germany at the moment but we will watch carefully," Issing told journalists.
Issing said talk about raising German interest rates would create the impression that inflation was a concern but said this was not the case.
"The weakness of the mark creates cost pressure but as long as that is accompanied by falling wage costs, that is offset," Issing said.
Issing made the comments at a seminar hosted by the Centre for European Reform, a British think-tank.
